description.narrative: The development objective of the Lao Landscapes and Livelihoods Project for Lao People's Democratic Republic (PDR) is to promote sustainable forest management, improve protected area management, and enhance livelihoods opportunities in selected landscapes in Lao PDR. The project comprises of four components. The first component, investing in natural wealth and resilience in forest landscapes objective is to build natural capital from improved forest landscape management. It consists of following sub-components: (i) protected areas and nature-based tourism; and (ii) sustainable forestry and resilient village infrastructure. The second component, livelihoods opportunities from sustainable forest landscapes objective is to improve forest-smart livelihoods opportunities, vocational skills, and nature-based tourism (NBT) development in targeted landscapes. It consists of following sub-components: (i) village livelihood block grants to village development funds; (ii) vocational training and skills development; and (iii) nature-based tourism business leveraging facility. The third component, institutions, incentives, and information objective are to strengthen institutions, policies, incentives, and information for sustainable forest landscapes. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthening institutions and policies for landscape management; (ii) strengthening institutions and policies to reduce forest and wildlife crimes; and (iii) information for decision support. The fourth component, project management and monitoring objective is to maintain and enhance project management, monitoring, and learning. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthens the capacity of Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and Department of Forestry (MAF and DOF) in project management, monitoring, evaluation, and coordination; and (ii) supports building partnerships, knowledge sharing with wider stakeholders, regional coordination and dialogues on project related issues, and resource mobilization.
To promote sustainable forest management, improve protected area management, and enhance livelihoods opportunities in selected landscapes in Lao PDR.

condition.narrative: IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.A.1(a) | Institutional Arrangements. The Recipient shall vest responsibility forthe overall implementation of the Project in DOF within MAF. To this end the Recipient, through MAF, shall not later than one (1)month after the Effective Date establish within MAF, and thereafter maintain throughout the implementation of the Project, theProject Coordination Units at the central, provincial and district levels for the purposes of day-to-day Project management andcoordination, with staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association.

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.A.1(b) | Institutional Arrangements. The Recipient, through MAF, shall not laterthan three (3) months after the Effective Date, appoint a BLF management contractor under terms of reference and withqualifications acceptable to the Association to support the implementation of Part 2.3 of the Project, and thereafter maintain thesaid contractor for such purpose at all times during the implementation of Part 2.3 of the Project.

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.A.1(c) | Institutional Arrangements. The Recipient, through MAF, shall not laterthan three (3) months after the Effective Date, enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with Ministry of National Defense settingout measures and actions that need to be taken to enable MAF to implement the Project within PKK, pursuant to the Prime MinisterOffice Notice No. 906/PMO dated August 21, 2020 on the transfer of the mandate of PKK management to MAF.

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.B.1 | Project Operations Manual. The Recipient shall through MAF ensure that theProject is carried out in accordance with the arrangements and procedures set out in the Project Operations Manual

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.D.1 | Environmental and Social Standards. The Recipient shall through MAF ensurethat the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable to theAssociation.

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.D.2 | Environmental and Social Standards. Without limitation upon paragraph 1above, the Recipient shall through MAF ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with the Environmental and SocialCommitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association. To this end, the Recipient shall through MAF ensure that:(a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented with due diligence and efficiency, and as further specified inthe ESCP; (b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP; (c) policies, procedures andqualified staff are maintained to enable it to implement the ESCP, as further specified in the ESCP; and (d) any of the ESCP, orany provision thereof, is not amended, revised or waived, except as the Association shall otherwise agree in writing and theRecipient has, thereafter, disclosed the revised ESCP.

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.E.1 | Block Grants and Matching Grants. The Recipient shall through MAF makeavailable Block Grants and Matching Grants to Beneficiaries in accordance with eligibility criteria, arrangements and proceduresacceptable to the Association as set out in the Project Operations Manual for the purpose of carrying out Sub-Projects under Parts2.1 and 2.3 respectively.

IDA Financing Agreement | Schedule 2 | Section I.E.2 | Block Grants and Matching Grants. The Recipient shall ensure that noSub-projects shall be eligible for financing from the proceeds of Block Grants and Matching Grants until MAF or its respectivelocal office has entered into a Grant Agreement with a respective Beneficiary, on terms and conditions acceptable to theAssociation, and shall obtain rights adequate to protect its interests and those of the Association.

The Recipient shall ensure that the following items are submitted to the Bank in a timely manner as indicated below:(a) AnnualWork Program and Budget which is due not later than June 30 of each year(b) Project report not later than 45 days after the end ofeach calendar semester

comment.narrative:
Baseline & Targets (2019-2022): Similar to Indicator 1, targets vary between “good” forests in LLL target villages and other areas. Good Forests (in LLL Target Villages): Expected emissions reduction from 0.40 million tonnes/year to 0.31 million tonnes/year. Other Areas: Emissions are expected to remain stable at 1.00 million tonnes/year. Overall LLL Landscapes: Projected emissions decline from 1.40 million tonnes/year to 1.31 million tonnes/year.
Expected Impact: The total cumulative reduction in emissions over the project period is estimated at 0.18 million tonnes.
Assumptions: Government policies do not have negative impact on remaining forest outside good forest. Provision of grants incentivize forest conservation and prevent leakage.

title.narrative: 15. Share of women members of the Village Committees' LLL Teams

comment.narrative:
Counted are all members in 1) all committees managing the VLDBG (note: names of committees might vary, depending on the scope of funds existing in the village, 2) village Forest and Livelihood Committee (established as part of Village committee LLL team), village Forest Committee, and livelihood Team.
Data on committee members is collected at CEE 2 and VLD 1 stages and entered into the system by Village Facilitators, the latest updated data is reported.
Notes: Double-counting of persons in several committees cannot be avoided. Committees don't only manage LLL activities, but also others.

title.narrative: 11. Tourism agreements signed between tourism operators, local villages and relevant PA and other management authorities in targeted forest landscapes

comment.narrative: The following types of Tourism Agreements are counted: BLF (needs to include "employment benefits for local communities"), Concession Agreements, Memorandums of Understanding, Management Contracts, Approved documents (Permits for Tourism Agreements not directly resulted from the project intervention) and etc.

title.narrative: 13. Households establishing and managing tree plantations

comment.narrative:
The indicator measures the number of households involved in establishing and managing tree plantations with support provided by the project.
Progress on indicator achievement is expected in 2024.

title.narrative: 1. Landscape area with maintained or increased forest cover

comment.narrative:
The revised indictor considers the main drivers of forest loss include permanent agriculture, shifting cultivation, infrastructure development, and other land-use changes.
The baseline is based on forest loss between 2019-2022, assuming the same drivers and intensity continue. Targets vary between areas prioritized for forest protection (“good” forests) and other areas within the LLL landscape.
“Landscape Area" is aggregation of different categories of State forests within the 5 LLL landscapes (PAD). Includes the territory of LLL target villages which is outside the state forest boundaries.
“Forest” includes forest (following the definition used in the (FREL/FRL) and plantations Forest does not include “Forestland” (defined according to National Forest Cover Assessment).
These targets are ambitious, especially since available data suggests that the overall rate of forest loss in Lao PDR may have increased between 2022 and 2024.
FIPD is preparing a assessment report.

title.narrative: 12. Villages entering partnership agreements with environmentally and socially sustainable tree plantation enterprises

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of villages that enter partnership agreements that have been facilitated as a result of project support.
Progress on indicator achievement is expected in 2024.

title.narrative: 17. New or revised laws, policies, and regulations drafted and submitted to relevant authority for approval

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the support provided by the project to the GoL to enhance legislation, policy, and regulations.
The Wildlife Law was submitted to the Government for approval on March 25, 2023. The Law is expected to be reviewed by the National Assembly by October 2023.
A Prime Minister's Decree on Protected Areas a revision of the 2010 Protected Areas Decree was approved in June 2023.
A new Prime Minister's Order on Forest Encroachment was issued in July 2023.

title.narrative: 3. Households or Economic Interest Groups engaged in alternative and/or improved traditional livelihood activities supported by the project

comment.narrative:
“Households” are groups of people, often a family, who live together under one roof within LLL villages. “Economic Interest Groups” are groups formally or informally formed around a specific economic activity, and often helps in marketing of the products through improved product design, facilitation of market access and business operation services. “Traditional livelihood activities” include 1) VLDBG (key activity), including USD 8000 (VDF) and the USD 2000 Fund for Most Vulnerable Households (MVH). Counted only first round of use of VLDBG is monitored/counted (data-source are village level reports for VLDBG) and 2) “Out-grower scheme” are legally sanctioned contracts between village households and private sector enterprises. Counted are only those contracts, in which LLL had an active input (note: "impacts on livelihoods, jobs and poverty survey" will estimate the % of contracts with LLL inputs)
477 villages received the MVH grant and 7,221 hhs in 427 villages received VDC loans

title.narrative: Forest area brought under management plans

comment.narrative:
“Supported” includes supporting of implementing: where plans need not be formally revised, but LLL supports their implementation, updating plans: where plans exist but need to be formally revised and where LLL contributes to the updating and developing new plans. "Forest Areas" that can be considered supported by the project are 8 Protected Area (PA) = Conservation Forest Management Plans (indicator 5a). Production Forest Area (PFA) Management Plans (indicator 5b) +11 PFAs. Protection Forest Area (PtFA) Management Plans (Indicator 5c) + 6 PtFAs.
Primary sources of data-collection are the Areas mentioned in respective Plans. Qualitative context information will be given by “Impact of Landscape governance modalities” and “Impact on Landscape valuation, and ecosystem services” surveys
The area of VFM plans under indicator 5d overlaps with the area-based forest management plans under indicators 5a, 5b and 5c, so their area is not counted.
PKK/signed, YNMPSs & LVLV plans/drafts

title.narrative: 10. Village conservation agreements approved and annually reported

comment.narrative:
Village Conservation Agreements (VCA) are binding between the relevant government authority and the Village Administration.
VCA can be prepared and approved after Community Action Plan (CAP)
All PA villages have CCAs.

title.narrative: 9. Productive assets built and maintained for improved resilience

comment.narrative:
Count infrastructure: small irrigation or multipurpose small reservoirs (9a), tourism or park management facilities (9b), roads (9c), slope stabilization, and small bridges or drainage.
LLL Project is implementing 7 sub-projects (1 completed) and a selected survey-design company is implementing 33 subprojects.

title.narrative: 14. Households using Village Development Funds for forest-smart livelihoods activities

comment.narrative: “Village Development Funds (VDF) for forest-smart livelihoods activities” are Village Livelihood Block Grants (VLDBG) (managed by the VDF)). Counted are the Total number of HHs receiving loans or grants from VLDBG, only counting HHs using the ‘first round’ until VDF (USD 8,000) and the Fund for Most Vulnerable Households (MVHs) (USD 2,000), (total VLDBG of USD 10,000) are exhausted. Not count HHs receiving funds beyond these 10,000 (i.e. revolving fund). (Data to be retrieved from village report of VLD and/or VLBG distribution records). MVH funds may be used for forest-smart livelihood activities or for other purposes (excluding prohibited activities (negative list)).

"Job-focused interventions” are 1) VLDBG 1st round grant beneficiaries household members (in LLL VLD target villages), 2) Vocational training grant direct beneficiaries (component 2.2), 3) Persons hired to do the restoration of forest, 4) Persons hired by contractors (note: only contractors from target villages) to build village infrastructure, and Tourism (according to Tourism Agreements). “Beneficiaries” are all persons within those households with at least 1 person participating in LLL interventions. (assumption of 5.5 household members is used = nation-wide statistical number members of households in rural Laos)
Excluded are 1) VLDBG grants for most vulnerable households (because these grants are often not used for economic activities), 2) Further rounds of VLDBG grant users of the VLD Fund, and 3) Indirect employment (persons hired by beneficiary VLDBG households) are not counted.
HH members (in LLL VLD target villages) break down in ethnicity.

title.narrative: 8. Beneficiaries using extension or outreach services

comment.narrative:
The indicator is calculated as number of participants (“beneficiaries”) who participated in an extension / outreach activities multiplied by 2 of persons per HH.
“Extension or Outreach activities” are: village level participants in extension (= outreach) activities by DAFO, PAFO, and/or other government/non-government agencies for: Forestry/Agricultural/other land-based activities, Introduction of new forest management plan, Update forestry law, Dissemination of forest regulation, Village level follow-up activities
As some individuals might participate in more than 1 of these activities, double-counting cannot be avoided. For activities with large number of participants, participation is not recorded per person, however number of participants are counted/estimated.
Community outreach campaigns and events: 32,360 (45% F). Outreach Campaign booths on significant days: 5,176 (44% F). Health Education: 2,854 (63% F). Dissemination_of_laws /regulations: 7,252 (40% F). Others: 1,17

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices

comment.narrative: Counted are areas (in ha) under “sustainable management practices”, which is counted, if the following practices are fulfilled: • FLUZ completed and data is being migrated to M&E system. • PDMS under implementation means 1) trainings have been provided to the implementing staff, 2) equipment for PDMS implementation is available, and 3) the implementers have the resources (budget from LLL) to implement.

title.narrative: 16. Share of target beneficiaries with a score ‘Satisfied’ or above on project interventions

comment.narrative: “Beneficiaries” are all Villagers in LLL target villages, who are direct beneficiaries of LLL project interventions. “Project interventions” are VLDBG, MVH, and VDF. Resilience Infrastructure (indicator 9): Small irrigation or multipurpose small reservoirs (9a), tourism or park management facilities (9b), roads (9c), slope stabilization, small bridges or drainage, and environmental management. Activities include Participation in consultations for construction activities: Ranger Stations and PA Offices. Involvement in FPIC, study tours / farmer to farmer exchange trips, vocational training, FLUZ, CAP / CCA, VFMCC (for PAs), FMP, tourism (BLF), and plantations. Beneficiaries will be identified in detail at the inception phase of LLL Perception Survey. Counted are % of respondents with a score ‘Satisfied’ or above on project interventions, results from the sample will be extrapolated by the total numbers of beneficiaries.
